newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO policemen arrested over alleged beating.
newsitem.headline: PLO policemen arrested over alleged beating.

text.p: Ten Palestinian police officers, including a colonel, have been arrested in connection with the suspected beating of a Gazan detained by PLO security men, a PLO official said on Thursday.

The Palestinian Centre for Human Rights said in a statement that Nasser al-Abed Radwan, 28, was in a coma at Gaza's Shifa hospital apparently from a blow to the head. It urged the Palestinian Authority to investigate.

"There are grounds to believe that citizen Nasser al-Abed Radwan was subjected to beating by members of Force 17 after he was detained in violation of procedures necessary under Palestinian law," the statement said.
The group said Radwan was detained on unspecified charges on June 23 at his home by two members of Force 17, a unit that guards Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Announcing the arrest of the 10 policemen, Major General Abdel-Razek al-Majaydeh, head of Palestinian security forces in Gaza, said: "President Arafat gave me direct responsibility to supervise the investigation."
He said they could face charges in a military court after the investigation is completed.
Human rights groups say about 12 Palestinians have died in detention since the Palestinian Authority took charge of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip under a 1993 peace deal with Israel.
